situations.check: corrected: Admin's 'Waiting on a brand' tab does include these collaborations (it lists every one whose second payment is waiting), but shows no stage and no day count for them

situations.title: She took the first payment and went quiet
situations.stage: Any step that waits on her after both signatures: sending her address, answering a visit time, checking the parcel, marking the shoot done, uploading content, making shop posts, posting after approval
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes; money is at risk on Pay for Content and Hybrid, products on Remote
situations.rules_say: There is no cancel button after signing; non-performance is a dispute the brand reports to INFLX. In settling it INFLX may return the locked money to the brand with a written reason.
situations.today_entry_point: none in almost every state - the brand's screens only wait: '{name} hasn't sent her content yet. She is being reminded every two days.' (BrandContentScreen.js:139-145), '{name} sends her delivery address first ... nothing to do yet' (BrandRemoteScreen.js:119-124). Only exception: Pay for Sale / Hybrid 'She hasn't posted it', once approved and the posting date has passed.
situations.today_effect: She is reminded every 48 hours; after the posting date both sides see a 'Delayed' label; no money moves and nothing is recorded as a problem. If she received a parcel and never checks it, the return can never become overdue, because overdue only counts from the day she marks the shoot done.
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Content and Hybrid: 25% already in her wallet (possibly withdrawn), 75% of the brand's money locked, and the INFLX campaign fee already charged on Pay for Content. Remote: the brand's products are with her and the courier cost is spent.
situations.gap: The brand cannot tell INFLX at these steps. Admin already has the tool 'Return locked money - the creator took the first payment and stopped', but no request can reach it.
possible_outcomes: INFLX reaches her and she carries on, with a new date if needed
Locked 75% returned to the brand; she keeps the first 25%; collaboration ends as Disputed
75% returned and the first 25% taken back from her wallet if it is still there
Products recalled or written off; her account paused

Is the first 25% ever taken back?
Is the INFLX campaign fee returned to the brand when she walks away?
What happens to her account?

situations.title: The brand signed and then never starts the shoot

situations.rules_say: If the brand stops after the agreement it is a dispute and INFLX handles it. The rules give no button and no number of days.
situations.today_entry_point: none - she sees 'No visit planned yet. {brand} will send a time and the store address.' (ShootScreen.js:103; copy10.js:153-154) or '{brand} haven't sent your products yet. Nothing for you to do.' (RemoteShootScreen.js:132-134; copy11.js:220).
situations.today_effect: It sits in the brand's list of things to do; store-visit reminders only begin once a plan has been sent (shootPlan.service.js:483). After the posting date both see 'Delayed' - and for a Store Visit no plan can be sent after that day at all (see 'the posting date has passed'). Nothing is recorded as a problem.
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Content and Hybrid: 25% with her, 75% of the brand's money locked with no way out for either side. Pay for Sale: none.
situations.gap: No button for her, and the rules do not say what she is owed when the brand walks away.
possible_outcomes: INFLX nudges and the brand starts
INFLX returns the locked 75% to the brand and closes; she keeps the first 25% for her time
INFLX releases a further part to her as compensation
Pay for Sale: closed with nothing owed

situations.title: They disagree about whether the store visit happened
situations.stage: Store Visit - after the agreed time has passed, or after she taps 'I've been to the store'
situations.applies_to: Store Visit; all three aims
situations.rules_say: A missed time blames nobody; the brand sends a new one. She marks that she attended and the brand confirms; if the brand does nothing for 3 days the shoot confirms itself, which is safe because it moves no money.
situations.today_entry_point: none - she sees 'Your next step opens when {brand} confirm the visit. We keep reminding them until they do.' (ShootScreen.js:131-135). The brand has 'Confirm the shoot is done' or 'She didn't come — send a new time', and after a missed time 'Send a new time' and 'Call {name}' (BrandShootScreen.js:213-230). She can phone the store contact from her plan.
situations.today_effect: In the app a visit never confirms itself: the self-confirmation was retired on the founder's instruction of 1 Oct (shootPlan.service.js:378-379, 412-413), so the rules text is what is out of date. Only the brand's tap opens her next step; the brand is reminded every 48 hours with no end. 'She didn't come' wipes her mark and reopens the time; it is written in the diary but she cannot object, and the server clears her mark before it checks the new time.
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Content and Hybrid: 75% locked and unable to move. Her travel cost is outside INFLX.
situations.gap: No report on either side and no proof of a visit; the rules text and the app say opposite things about self-confirmation.
possible_outcomes: INFLX confirms the visit in the brand's place and the content step opens
A new time is agreed and the visit is repeated
Repeated no-show by her: locked money returned to the brand
Brand refuses to confirm without a reason: INFLX confirms
open_questions: Correct the rules to 'only the brand confirms', or bring back a self-confirmation with a longer wait?
What counts as proof of a visit - a photo at the store, a code from the store?
How many missed visits before it counts as not doing the job?
situations.check: corrected: the app's 'never confirms itself' is a recorded founder decision (1 Oct), so the rules need the correction; she is not without contact (she can phone the store contact); added that her mark is cleared before the new time is checked

situations.title: A report has been made - and then nothing can happen
situations.stage: Any collaboration after 'Report to INFLX', 'Tell INFLX' or 'Ask INFLX to look' has been tapped
situations.raised_by: brand or creator, both now waiting on INFLX
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes
situations.rules_say: Disputed is a state after signing; a dispute runs Disputed -> INFLX Resolution -> Resolved/Closed. Admin may manage and record the outcome; the detailed Admin dispute screens are deferred.
situations.today_entry_point: none for anything that follows - the reporter sees a card 'Reported to INFLX ... INFLX has it' (BrandContentScreen.js:129-130), the other side 'They told INFLX ... INFLX will contact you both' (ContentScreen.js:253-254). No reply box, no way to add proof, no way to take it back, no progress shown.
situations.today_effect: A brand's content report freezes the step and no code ever clears the mark (searched backend/src for brand_reported_at - it is only set and read). No admin is notified; no admin page lists reports, reasons or notes; the only hint is one sentence in the release pop-up ('The brand reported this collaboration'). Through the money tools a frozen collaboration can end two ways: INFLX releases both payments by hand and it becomes Completed, or INFLX returns the locked money - then only the brand is notified, the status never changes, and both screens keep saying 'reported' (the brand's reads '₹0 of her fee stays in escrow until it is settled'). In lists the collaboration shows a 'Waiting' chip.
situations.money_at_stake: Whatever was locked stays locked with INFLX indefinitely (up to 75% of a fee). Pay for Sale: nothing is held; her posts keep selling.
situations.gap: The whole middle of a dispute is missing: a queue for INFLX, the other side's answer, proof, a decision with its reason, lifting the freeze or ending the collaboration, telling both sides, and a final state both can see. A Pay for Sale report has no money row, so it appears nowhere in Admin at all.
possible_outcomes: Resolved - carry on: freeze lifted, normal flow resumes
Resolved - creator paid: locked payments released to her
Resolved - money returned to the brand
Resolved - split between them
Withdrawn by the person who reported
Closed - settled outside INFLX and recorded
open_questions: How quickly does INFLX promise to respond, and is that shown on the screen?
May the reporter withdraw a report?
Does the other side get a right to reply, with a deadline?
Is INFLX's decision final, or is there one appeal?
Should both sides see a 'Disputed' label instead of 'Waiting'?
situations.check: corrected: a frozen collaboration is not strictly endless - INFLX's money tools can complete it or return the money - but after a return the screens still say 'reported', the creator is not told and the status never changes; the 'INFLX settled it' screens show only when there is no brand report

situations.title: Something goes wrong after the content was confirmed live
situations.stage: During the wait for the final 50%, or after the collaboration is Completed - for example she deletes the post, takes a shop post down, or the brand uses her content beyond the agreed usage rights
situations.applies_to: Pay for Content and Hybrid (final payment); all aims for usage rights
situations.rules_ref: rules v1.31 §12.2 line 637; §26 line 904; §13 lines 667-669; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md line 453
situations.rules_say: Nothing is checked again in that week; whether the content stays up is governed by the agreement's usage terms. Any other material breach is a dispute. The two rules documents disagree on shop posts: the master rules say she cannot delete a live shoppable post, the offer rules say she can take a post down herself.
situations.today_entry_point: none - once the brand has confirmed, its screen has no report (the server offers 'posted wrongly' only before confirmation, contentFlow.service.js:336). She has nowhere to report misuse of her content.
situations.today_effect: The final 50% is paid by the nightly job on its date; only a brand report made before confirmation would stop it. She can take an approved or live shop post down herself; the diary records it and the brand is not told (shoppablePosts.service.js:868-877).
situations.money_at_stake: The final 50% of her fee, queued with INFLX for up to 7 days; after completion nothing is held. Future commission on a post that is taken down.
situations.gap: No button for either side, no way to pause the final payment, and no rule on how long a post must stay up.
possible_outcomes: Nothing: the rules as written do not check again
INFLX holds the final 50% while it looks
Final 50% returned to the brand
Noted on the account; settled outside INFLX
open_questions: Must the content stay up for a minimum time, and is the final 50% tied to that?
Does INFLX police usage rights at all, or only record a complaint?
May she take a live shop post down - which of the two rules documents is right?
situations.check: corrected: added that the two rules documents disagree on whether she may take a live shop post down (the app follows the offer rules); the rest confirmed

situations.title: The brand disagrees with a shopper's return, replacement or refund
situations.stage: Shopper order after delivery - when a return is requested, approved, or the item is collected
situations.applies_to: Every order placed from a shoppable post
situations.rules_say: The brand sees the return and is told; it does not decide. It brings a replacement and collects the other item at its own cost. A damaged item is not put back on sale.
situations.today_entry_point: none - the website's Returns page is marked 'View only — our team processes approvals & refunds' (dashboard/returns/page.js:109-114) and the brand's returns route is read-only (returns.routes.js:9-18). Only a replacement has buttons, 'Mark sent' and 'Mark delivered' (dashboard/fulfillment/page.js:254-256).
situations.today_effect: The brand is told 'Collect it from the shopper and tell INFLX when it is back' but has no button to say so; INFLX's admin marks the refund. Nothing the brand thinks about the returned item is recorded.
situations.money_at_stake: The brand's share of the sale (waiting, then reversed), the item itself, and the brand's cost of collecting or replacing.
situations.gap: The brand cannot say 'it came back used or damaged', 'the shopper did not hand it over' or 'it was fine when it left', and cannot confirm the item is back.
possible_outcomes: Refund stands; the brand bears the loss
Refund refused because the item is not in returnable condition; the sale stands
INFLX pays the shopper as goodwill and the brand keeps its share
Shopper marked for return abuse
open_questions: Does the brand get a say before INFLX approves 'damaged' or 'not as shown'?
Who bears the loss when a returned item is unusable?
Who confirms the item is back - the brand with a button, or INFLX by phone?

situations.title: Money in the wallet is not what the person expected, or a withdrawal does not arrive
situations.stage: Wallet - a withdrawal still waiting past the promised time, marked Processed but not in the bank, or a payment, commission or added money that looks wrong
situations.applies_to: All aims
situations.rules_say: A request is processed within 24 hours; INFLX pays from its bank, records the reference and marks it Processed. If it cannot pay it marks Could not process with the reason and the hold is released. Admin can repair an uncredited payment and correct a balance, each with a written reason.
situations.today_entry_point: none - the Withdraw screen promises 'INFLX pays this within {h} hours' (copy17.js:138-139) and the list shows Waiting, Processed with its reference, or Could not process with its reason (WithdrawalsScreen.js:42-52). No row has 'I didn't receive this' or 'ask about this'.
situations.today_effect: Nothing is recorded. Admin has the repair tools (credit a payment that was not credited, correct a balance) but a request has only two actions, Processed and Could not process, and a Processed one cannot be reopened.
situations.money_at_stake: The requested amount: on hold in the wallet until paid; after 'Processed' it has left the wallet and should be in the bank.
situations.gap: No way to question a wallet row or a late or missing withdrawal from inside the app (searched every wallet screen for report, help, contact, support - not found).
possible_outcomes: INFLX shows the bank reference and the person finds the money
INFLX pays again and records it
INFLX puts the amount back by balance correction and the person requests again
Explained; no change
open_questions: Does a money question get its own button on each wallet row, or go through one general 'Tell INFLX'?
What does the person see when 'within 24 hours' is missed?

situations.title: Any other broken promise - there is no general way to tell INFLX from inside the apps
situations.stage: Anywhere after signing or after an order is placed
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes; all shopper orders
situations.rules_say: 'Other material violation of signed agreement - affected party - Dispute Resolution.' My orders is meant to carry 'Need help'.
situations.today_entry_point: none on any work screen. Brand and creator: Profile > 'Legal & policies' (BrandProfileScreen.js:129; influencer/ProfileScreen.js:130). Shopper: Profile > 'Policies and help - Returns, privacy, terms' (shop/ProfileScreen.js:109). These open documents, including Grievance Redressal and Contact, which give INFLX's email and phone number as plain text.
situations.today_effect: Nothing is recorded inside INFLX. The website has /contact and /legal/grievance, whose form only composes an email ('no complaints endpoint on the backend yet'); the brand's website dashboard links to neither. Several sentences send people to INFLX with no button behind them: 'If something has gone wrong, tell INFLX' (cancelling a signed campaign), 'If something looks wrong, tell INFLX', 'Please contact INFLX and we will sort it out', 'This account is suspended. Contact support.' The in-app policy says every post, listing, offer, review and profile has a report option while only comments do.
situations.money_at_stake: Depends on the case - whatever is locked or pending at that moment stays where it is.
situations.gap: A single 'Tell INFLX about this' on every collaboration and every order, with a reason, a note and proof, tied to that collaboration or order. The reason written in the code for leaving 'Need help' out (no support contact yet) no longer holds: the support email and mobile are now published.
possible_outcomes: It turns out to be one of the named situations and follows that path
Answered as a help question; no dispute opened
Recorded as a breach and decided by INFLX with a money outcome
open_questions: One general button on every collaboration and order, or only the specific buttons at specific steps?
Is a phone or WhatsApp help line the first step before a formal report?
Should the policy text be corrected, or the promised report options built?
situations.check: corrected: added two more sentences that send people to INFLX with no button (settled order, suspended account); added that the support email and mobile are now published, so the stated reason for leaving 'Need help' out is gone

situations.title: The posting date has passed and a store visit can no longer be given a time
situations.stage: Store Visit shoot plan, from the day after the Set's posting date
situations.raised_by: brand or creator (neither can raise it today)
situations.against: whichever side let the date pass
situations.applies_to: Store Visit; all three aims
situations.rules_say: No visit time later than the posting date is offered - yet a Delayed collaboration's shoot plan 'stays fully usable' and every open step stays open. The two sentences cannot both hold; the code follows the first.
situations.today_entry_point: none. The brand's Delayed screen still shows 'Plan the visit' or 'Send a new time' (BrandShootScreen.js:207-216) and says 'You can still plan a visit and carry on' (copy10.js:228); her screen says '{brand} will send a new time' (copy10.js:152).
situations.today_effect: Every new time is refused with 'The visit has to be before {date}, her last day to go live' (shootPlan.service.js:128-136, 253; negotiation.service.js:260-268 - no exception for a Delayed collaboration was found), and shoot reminders stop after the posting date unless she has already marked the visit (shootPlan.service.js:488). If a time was agreed earlier she can still mark the visit and the brand can confirm; if no plan was ever sent, nothing can move.
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Content and Hybrid: 25% with her and 75% of the brand's money locked, with no step able to release or return it. Pay for Sale: none.
situations.gap: The screens promise a new time the server will not accept, there is no cancel after signing, and neither side has a report button - a complete stop.
possible_outcomes: Allow visit times after the posting date once a collaboration is Delayed
INFLX sets a new posting date for that one collaboration
INFLX returns the locked 75% to the brand and closes it
INFLX marks the visit done by hand after the two settle it between them
open_questions: After the posting date, may a visit still be planned - and until when?
If the brand never sent a plan in time, who is at fault and what is she owed?

situations.title: A parcel is lost or stuck with the courier - on its way to her, or on its way back
situations.stage: Remote shoot - after the courier collects the parcel, or after the return pickup is booked
situations.against: the courier (booked from INFLX's own courier account)
situations.applies_to: Remote only; all three aims
situations.rules_ref: not in the rules (§11.2 lines 516-519 cover only failed delivery attempts, a parcel brought back to the store, and weight charges)
situations.rules_say: The rules describe a parcel the courier brings back to the store (the brand may book once more) but say nothing about a parcel that never arrives anywhere.
situations.today_entry_point: none. Until the courier says Delivered she sees tracking only (RemoteShootScreen.js:141-166); the brand sees tracking and cannot cancel once the parcel is collected (remoteShoot.service.js:325-326). For a return on its way the brand sees only '{name}'s return is on its way back' (BrandRemoteScreen.js:322-324).
situations.today_effect: Nothing is recorded. She cannot check the items until the courier marks Delivered, so she cannot mark the shoot done and the content step never opens. A booked return is never 'overdue', and the brand can neither confirm nor report it until it is marked delivered. If the courier says Delivered but she got nothing, her only route is to mark every item Missing.
situations.money_at_stake: The courier charge already taken from the brand's wallet, the return-pickup money still locked, and the products. On Pay for Content and Hybrid the 75% stays locked because the shoot cannot be marked done.
situations.gap: No 'it never arrived' button for either side, no courier claim process, and no way to send a second parcel (a re-booking is allowed only after the courier brings the first one back).
possible_outcomes: INFLX raises a claim with the courier and credits the brand's wallet with what is recovered
INFLX returns the courier charge to the brand by balance correction
INFLX allows a second parcel for that collaboration
INFLX opens the content step by hand so she can work from what she has
open_questions: Who chases the courier - INFLX (its account) or the brand?
Does the brand get the shipping money back, and the value of the products?
After how many days without movement is a parcel treated as lost?

situations.title: A shopper is owed a refund and it has not reached her
situations.stage: After she or the brand cancels an item before shipping, or after a return is marked refunded
situations.applies_to: Every order placed from a shoppable post; online and cash on delivery
situations.rules_say: An online payment is refunded automatically to the original payment method. A returned cash-on-delivery order 'is paid back by INFLX by hand'.
situations.today_entry_point: none. She reads 'Refund of ₹X to your original payment method in 5–7 working days', 'We couldn't start the refund. INFLX will sort it out and tell you.' or 'You paid cash, so INFLX sends your refund of ₹X to you directly.' (copyOrder.js:214-216; copyReturn.js:34) - none has a button.
situations.today_effect: A refund that fails is only marked on the item and written to the server log (shopperOrders.service.js:502-506; shopperReturns.service.js:367-371): no admin is notified and no admin page lists failed refunds (searched Packages/brand-web/app/admin - the only mention is one line shown at 'Mark refunded', admin/returns/page.js:332). The app never asks a cash shopper where to send her money, and nothing records that a by-hand refund was paid.
situations.money_at_stake: What she paid for the item. For an online order INFLX holds it; for a cash order the cash never reached INFLX (see the cash-on-delivery situation).
situations.gap: No way for her to chase a refund, no list for INFLX of refunds that failed or are owed by hand, and no place to collect her UPI or bank details.
possible_outcomes: INFLX retries the online refund and tells her
INFLX pays by hand to a UPI or bank account she gives, and records the reference
INFLX shows her the refund reference so she can ask her bank
open_questions: How does INFLX collect UPI or bank details for a cash refund?
Who at INFLX watches for failed refunds, and how soon must they be fixed?
Should she see a refund reference and a 'not received' button after the promised days?

situations.title: The brand ends the offer or takes its products off sale, and her posts leave the shop
situations.stage: Any time after her shoppable posts are approved - including after the collaboration is Completed
situations.applies_to: Pay for Sale and Hybrid
situations.rules_ref: Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md 4.9 lines 455-465; rules v1.31 §20 lines 813-817; §19 line 806
situations.rules_say: A post is removed when its offer ends (by date or early), or when its products leave the offer, become unavailable or sell out; the creator is notified. Selling is meant to continue while products are available, and a brand 'does not manually close a healthy sale collaboration simply because it is selling'.
situations.today_entry_point: none. She gets a notification with the reason and the post reads 'Removed' (shoppablePosts.service.js:970-985); searched the creator's post and Going live screens for report / tell INFLX / ask INFLX - not found.
situations.today_effect: Removal is final for that post and her commission on it stops. The brand needs no reason, INFLX is not told, and nothing is recorded as a problem.
situations.money_at_stake: No locked money - her future commission on those posts. Commission already earned is not touched.
situations.gap: She cannot say 'the brand did this to stop paying me', and no rule says how long an offer must run or what notice she is owed.
possible_outcomes: Nothing: ending an offer or stock is the brand's right
The brand must give a reason, which she and INFLX can see
A minimum selling period is promised in the agreement
INFLX restores the post as a price post where the products are still on sale
open_questions: Is a brand free to end an offer or pull products at any time, or does she get a minimum selling period?
Does INFLX want to see when a brand removes products right after a collaboration completes?

situations.title: On a cash-on-delivery order the cash is with the brand, but INFLX's records treat it as held by INFLX
situations.stage: Shopper order paid in cash - from delivery to the close of the return window, and whenever a cash order is refunded
situations.raised_by: INFLX (or the brand, when it is asked to pay money back)
situations.applies_to: Every cash-on-delivery order from a shoppable post (cash is on by default, up to ₹5,000)
situations.rules_ref: rules v1.31 §17A line 777; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md lines 1081-1084 (the two disagree)
situations.rules_say: Master rules: INFLX collects the cash through the delivery partner and the brand owes INFLX nothing. Offer rules: the brand's courier collects the cash and the brand owes INFLX the creator's and INFLX's shares, taken from its next payouts.
situations.today_entry_point: none - it is not a button; it is what the screens and the books say. The brand website tells the brand: 'Cash on delivery: you collect ₹X. The creator's and INFLX's shares are taken from your next online payout.' (dashboard/fulfillment/page.js:332-334).
situations.today_effect: The brand ships with its own courier (dashboard/fulfillment/page.js:349-365), so the cash reaches the brand. When the return window closes the server adds the brand's share to its wallet and the creator's commission to hers exactly as for an online order, and records nothing owed by the brand (settlement.service.js:53-55, 84-109; the only code that writes an amount owed is for courier charges, remoteMoney.service.js:108). A returned cash order is refunded 'by INFLX by hand'.

existing_machinery.name: Content report record
existing_machinery.what: Each collaboration's content record already stores a brand report (when, who, reason, note up to 500 characters) and a creator report (when, who, note), plus the stamped date from which she may ask. existing_machinery.what: One server function takes the report from either side, checks it is allowed at that step, records it once, notifies both sides and writes the diary. A brand report freezes every later action, stops reminders, stops the Pay for Sale self-confirmation and stops the final payment job. Nothing ever lifts the freeze.

existing_machinery.name: Remote parcel report record and endpoint
existing_machinery.what: Three report dates on the shoot (difference, return problem, return overdue) and one endpoint that records each once and writes the diary; it already accepts a note, but the app sends none. The 'return problem' kind works on the server but has no button; a per-item report date exists in the database and is never written.

existing_machinery.name: Report pop-ups on the phone
existing_machinery.what: Three ready pop-ups: content report with a note box, Pay for Sale report with a list of reasons plus a note box, and the Remote report (no note box, one body text for all three kinds). Also the 'reported' cards each side sees afterwards.

existing_machinery.name: Admin > Money > Disputes and corrections
existing_machinery.what: Three by-hand money tools, each needing a written reason and each logged with who did it: release the next locked payment to the creator (and, when she has posted and the brand has not reported, confirm live in the brand's place so the final 50% pays itself), return everything still locked to the brand, and add to or take from one wallet. Releasing tells both sides; returning tells only the brand; a balance correction notifies nobody (it shows in the person's History).

existing_machinery.name: Admin > Money > Collaboration money
existing_machinery.what: Lists every Pay for Content and Hybrid collaboration with money locked, including a 'Waiting on a brand' tab (every collaboration whose second payment waits on the brand, with days since she posted once she has). The server sends a 'reported' flag with each row; this page does not show it - only the release pop-up uses it.

existing_machinery.name: Screens for 'INFLX settled it'
existing_machinery.what: Both apps already show the result when INFLX moves money by hand: 'INFLX confirmed your content is live', 'INFLX has settled this payment', 'INFLX returned the locked amount to the brand', and the brand's confirm button is refused in plain words afterwards. They appear only when there is no brand report on the collaboration - a frozen one keeps its 'reported' card.

existing_machinery.name: Admin link to disputed content files
existing_machinery.what: An admin-only link that opens a collaboration's content files, allowed only once either side has reported. No admin page uses it yet.

existing_machinery.name: The collaboration diary
existing_machinery.what: One record of everything that happened in a collaboration, step by step, with who did it (brand, creator, admin, system) - reports, confirmations, shoot and parcel steps and INFLX's money actions are already written to it. Reading is only exposed for the negotiation stage, and a ready 'what happened here' list component exists but no screen uses it.

existing_machinery.name: Notifications for reports
existing_machinery.what: Notification types already exist for 'reported to INFLX' on content and on going live, and for a parcel difference. The shopper-returns code already has the pattern of notifying every admin; collaboration reports do not use it.

existing_machinery.name: Admin settings stamped on each collaboration
existing_machinery.what: Admin numbers that already shape disputes: content change rounds (2), days of brand silence before she may ask (7), final payment wait (7), Remote return window (7), Remote return self-confirm (7), Pay for Sale self-confirm (7). existing_machinery.name: 'Disputed' words already reserved
existing_machinery.what: The database already allows 'disputed' as a status for a locked payment and for an agreement, and the app has a 'Disputed' chip label, but nothing ever sets any of them. A reported collaboration shows as 'Waiting' today.

existing_machinery.name: Shopper returns, replacements and one-item refunds
existing_machinery.what: A complete request-decide-refund path: the shopper asks with a reason, every admin is notified, INFLX's Admin > Returns approves or rejects with a note she is shown, the sale's three shares wait meanwhile, and a refund reverses them. existing_machinery.name: Clocks that end silence without a dispute

existing_machinery.name: Reported comments queue

existing_machinery.name: Legal, grievance and contact pages - and a published support contact

existing_machinery.name: Agreement wording and the no-cancel guard
existing_machinery.what: Every agreement already says disputes follow the INFLX dispute process, and the server refuses to cancel a campaign once any collaboration in it is signed by both, with the words 'If something has gone wrong, tell INFLX.'

result.area: Behaviour disputes — conduct that is not one step of a collaboration (usage rights, deleted posts, fake numbers, handle changes, harassment, going off-platform, suspended or deleted accounts, blocks, self-dealing, bad shop posts, comment reports, return abuse, lapsed plans, pulled offers)
result.summary: The master rules cover almost none of this area: section 26 lists step failures plus one catch-all line ("other material violation of signed agreement"), and a word search of both rule documents finds nothing on suspension, account deletion, harassment, fake numbers, paid-post labels, exclusivity or dealing outside INFLX. The code matches that silence: there is no dispute record, nothing ever sets a collaboration or a locked payment to "Disputed", and a "Report to INFLX" today reaches nobody at INFLX — no admin is alerted, the note typed with it is saved and never shown again, and the only trace is a yes/no mark on Admin › Money › Collaborations. Reusable pieces exist but are scattered: silent blocks, suspend/reinstate, the shopper comment-report queue, three admin money tools, and an agreement that stamps usage rights, her handle, who signed and from which device, and a terms version; the shared diary is written for signed collaborations and shop posts but no screen or endpoint reads it back. Three findings matter most: (1) once a brand confirms a post is live it cannot stop the final 50% if she deletes the post during the wait; (2) suspending an account only locks that person's own collaboration buttons — the other side is told nothing and waits forever, the posts keep selling and money keeps arriving; (3) the two rule documents disagree on whether she may take a live shop post down, and a taken-down post still counts toward her minimum. Promises already made outside the product are unmet: the standard terms stamped on every agreement (version 1.0 as seeded) say disputes are "resolved through the INFLX platform dispute resolution process", and the published legal pages promise payout holds during an investigation, closing an account from settings, and an 18+ rule, none of which the product does; the grievance form is only an email hand-off. Rules line numbers refer to C:/Users/aveen/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--WORK/8589ae7a-400f-4ed9-85e4-2d125cefbee6/scratchpad/rules131.txt.

A signed collaboration abandoned to continue offline is handled as 'stopped after signing', which section 26 already names
open_questions: Do you want a rule against it at all at this stage?
If yes, for how long after an introduction, and what would count as proof?
Does it apply to both sides equally?

situations.title: INFLX suspends a brand or creator while a collaboration is running, money is locked, or money is in the wallet
situations.stage: Any time after signing; also while shopper orders are on the way or sales are inside the return window
situations.raised_by: INFLX (admin); the one harmed is the other side
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes; shopper orders for Pay for Sale and Hybrid
situations.rules_ref: not in the rules (searched for suspend and deactivate: no match; section 5A line 187 only says a removed creator drops out of groups)
situations.rules_say: Silent. The published Brand Agreement says a suspension does not cancel what is owed to creators or shoppers; the Terms say INFLX can hold a payout while it investigates.
situations.today_entry_point: Admin › Brands / Influencers › Suspend — C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/controllers/admin.controller.js:128-212 and 218-306. The screen insists on a reason; the server does not, and the reason is wiped when the account is reinstated.
situations.today_effect: Only the account's status changes. That person gets a notification and SMS without the reason, and every collaboration step of theirs is refused (negotiation, agreement, shoot, Remote, content, going live). The other side is told nothing and simply waits — only the brand can confirm a store visit or confirm content live. Money jobs, the shop feed and checkout never look at account status, so the final 50%, commission and sale shares keep arriving and their posts keep selling. A suspended creator cannot ask to withdraw or take a post down; a suspended brand can still withdraw and still handle shopper orders.
situations.money_at_stake: Locked fee portions; both wallets' Available; sale shares inside the return window; shoppers' paid orders not yet delivered. All held by INFLX.
situations.gap: A decided checklist for a suspension: each active collaboration, posts in the shop, open orders, locked money, the wallet; telling the other side; clocks that run out while the suspended side cannot act; the suspend screen shows no count of active work; no history of past suspensions is kept.
possible_outcomes: Suspension blocks new work only; signed work may be finished
INFLX settles each active collaboration by hand: creator suspended — locked money back to the brand; brand suspended — release for work done, return the rest
Posts hidden from the shop while suspended and restored on reinstatement
Wallet frozen during the investigation, then paid out or kept back according to the finding
open_questions: Does a suspension freeze signed collaborations or only stop new ones?
Do the suspended party's posts leave the shop?
Is the wallet frozen — today a creator is blocked from withdrawing and a brand is not?
Who tells the other side, and in what words?
What happens to shoppers' undelivered orders from a suspended brand?
If the suspended side misses a date it could not act on, whose fault is it?
situations.check: corrected: the reason is required on the screen but not by the server, is not sent to anyone and is wiped on reinstatement; every collaboration step of the suspended side is refused so the other side is stuck; a suspended brand can still withdraw and handle shopper orders

situations.title: A brand or creator asks to delete the account while a collaboration is active or money is still with INFLX
situations.stage: Any time
situations.raised_by: brand or creator; the one harmed is the other side
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes
situations.rules_say: Silent. The published 'Delete My Account' page says: withdraw your balance first, signed campaigns must still be completed, and if a dispute, payout or order blocks deletion INFLX will say so. The Terms say an account can be closed 'from your settings'.
situations.today_entry_point: none in the apps or the backend (searched backend/src, the phone app and the website for delete/close-account: only the legal page text). Requests come by email, phone or the grievance email form.
situations.today_effect: There is no code path; whatever happens is done by hand. Nothing checks for active collaborations, locked money or a wallet balance first.
situations.money_at_stake: Wallet Available, money locked in collaborations, commission and sale shares inside the return window.
situations.gap: A rule and a checklist: refuse or delay deletion while anything is open; what happens to leftover wallet money; whether her posts leave the shop; the Terms' 'close it from your settings' has nothing behind it.
possible_outcomes: Deletion waits until every collaboration is complete and the wallet is withdrawn
INFLX settles each active collaboration as a dispute, pays out the wallet, then deletes
Money nobody claims is kept under a stated policy
open_questions: Is deletion refused while a collaboration is active?
What happens to money left in the wallet of a deleted account?
Do her posts leave the shop on deletion — and if so what does the brand get back on a Hybrid fee?

situations.title: A creator who owns the brand collaborates with herself, or someone buys through their own post to earn commission
situations.stage: At invitation and signing, and at every sale
situations.applies_to: Pay for Sale and Hybrid mostly (commission); any aim for a self-collaboration
situations.rules_say: One person may be both a brand owner and a creator; she can 'connect/verify the Brand using the Brand credentials' and the two identities stay distinct. Nothing about commission on her own brand's sales. The published Terms forbid 'placing orders through your own storefront' to manipulate commission.
situations.today_entry_point: none
situations.today_effect: One phone number can hold a brand account and a creator account, each with its own wallet. The 'connect my brand' link of section 2 is not stored anywhere, and nothing stops the brand inviting its owner or a creator buying through her own post (searched invitation, eligibility and checkout code for a same-person check: none). The migration that allowed this says those rules were left for a later stage.
situations.money_at_stake: The commission on those sales — it comes out of the brand's own share, so mostly the owner paying herself; INFLX still keeps its share.
situations.gap: A decision on whether it matters. If it does: store the link (same phone number) and flag it.
possible_outcomes: Allowed; not a dispute
Allowed, but no commission on her own brand's sales
Self-purchases found: that commission is taken back by a written correction and a warning recorded
open_questions: May a creator collaborate with a brand she owns?
Does she earn commission on her own brand's sales?
Is buying through your own post a breach that costs the commission?

situations.title: A shoppable post INFLX already approved turns out to be offensive, misleading, to use someone else's music or pictures, or to make a false claim about the product
situations.stage: After the post is live in the shop
situations.raised_by: brand, shopper, an outsider whose work was used, or INFLX
situations.against: creator (or the brand, if the claim came from it)
situations.applies_to: Pay for Sale and Hybrid
situations.rules_ref: Section 13 lines 663-671; section 26 line 903; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md sections 4.7-4.8 lines 442 and 453
situations.rules_say: INFLX checks quality (and copyrighted music) before approval; after approval there are no edits; a brand's disagreement about the social version does not remove the live shop post. Nothing about removing an approved post for something found later.
situations.today_entry_point: none. Admin can only approve or send back a post that is waiting for review — C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/creatorPosts.service.js:342-360. No brand or shopper 'report this post'; an outsider has only the grievance email form.
situations.today_effect: The post stays in the shop until its offer ends, its products go, or she takes it down herself. The system has no 'removed by INFLX' reason, and suspending her account does not hide it. Shoppers can report a comment but not a post.
situations.money_at_stake: Commission from sales through that post (waiting in the return window or already in her wallet); shoppers' orders made on a false claim.
situations.gap: An INFLX take-down with a reason; a report-a-post entry for the brand and for shoppers; what happens to her commission and to her minimum-post count.
possible_outcomes: INFLX removes the post; commission already earned stays
INFLX removes it and she must make a replacement to keep her minimum
Sales made on a false claim are undone through the normal returns route
Repeated: the creator is suspended
open_questions: May INFLX remove a post it already approved, and on whose report?
Does a post removed by INFLX still count toward her minimum?
Is commission earned through a post later judged misleading kept or taken back?
May the brand ask for removal of a post made for it?

situations.title: A shopper abuses returns — returns again and again, sends back a worn or different item, or falsely says it was damaged
situations.stage: After delivery, inside the return window
situations.raised_by: brand (it bears the loss); the creator loses her commission
situations.applies_to: Shopper orders from Pay for Sale and Hybrid posts
situations.rules_ref: Master rules section 18 lines 794-801; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md section 6.16 lines 1105-1140
situations.rules_say: INFLX decides every return: approve, or reject with a note. The brand sees it and is told but does not decide. One answer per item. Nothing about abuse or about the brand objecting.
situations.today_entry_point: Shopper: Return / Return or replace → Admin › Returns approves or rejects (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/shopperReturns.service.js:203 and 250). Brand: a read-only list of returns; nothing to object with.
situations.today_effect: The request is saved with a reason and an optional note; the sale's three shares wait while it is open; on refund the item is undone and the money returned. No photo is asked for, admin is not shown the shopper's past returns, nothing limits repeats, and admin cannot restrict a shopper (status changes exist for brand, creator and agency only; cash on delivery is one switch for everyone). The brand is told to collect the item and 'tell INFLX when it is back' — outside the app; there is no step where it confirms the item or its condition.
situations.money_at_stake: The item's price, held by INFLX; the creator's commission and the brand's share still waiting; the refund INFLX pays the shopper.
situations.gap: Photo proof for 'damaged' or 'not as shown'; the brand's word on whether and in what condition the item came back; the shopper's return history; a way to restrict a shopper.
possible_outcomes: INFLX rejects the return: the shares are added when the window closes
Approved, but the item comes back unusable: the brand reports it and INFLX decides who bears the loss
A repeat abuser loses cash on delivery, loses returns, or is blocked
open_questions: Who bears the loss when INFLX approved a return and the item comes back unusable — the brand, INFLX or the shopper?
May the brand object before INFLX decides?
Is a photo required for damaged or not-as-shown?
Is there a limit on returns per shopper?
situations.check: corrected: added that the brand has no in-app way to say the item came back or in what condition — INFLX marks it refunded on the brand's word

situations.title: The brand ends the offer early or takes the products off sale while her posts are live
situations.stage: After her posts are live, often after she has also shared them on social media
situations.applies_to: Pay for Sale and Hybrid
situations.rules_ref: Master rules section 20 lines 812-817; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md section 2.8 lines 290-297 and section 4.9 lines 457-465
situations.rules_say: Treated as a normal event, not a dispute: her posts leave the shop, she is notified and selling ends. The products inside an offer she holds are frozen, but the brand may still end the offer or take a product off sale. The master rules add that a brand 'does not manually close a healthy sale collaboration'.
situations.today_entry_point: Brand: 'End offer now' (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/offerLife.service.js:420-441) and unpublishing a product. The website's older 'End campaign' button also still exists (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/controllers/campaign.controller.js:1492-1605). Creator: nothing to object with.
situations.today_effect: Her posts leave the shop at once and for good; she gets a notification with the reason. Commission on sales already made is untouched. The older End campaign button is refused while money is locked or content awaits review, so it is open mainly to commission-only campaigns; it tells creators their products are no longer listed, which the new shop feed does not act on (whether a campaign made the new way can reach that button was not verified).
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Sale: nothing locked — she loses future commission after doing the work. Hybrid: her fixed fee is unaffected.
situations.gap: Nothing, if this is simply the brand's right. If not: a promised minimum selling period, or a consequence when a brand ends an offer within days of her post going live, and a way for her to say so. The old End campaign button needs a decision either way.
possible_outcomes: Leave as it is — commission-only risk is hers; not a dispute
A minimum live period is written into the agreement; ending earlier is the brand's breach, recorded, with a set compensation from the brand's wallet
A pattern across creators: the brand is warned or suspended
open_questions: Is ending an offer early always the brand's right, even the day after she posts?
Do you want a minimum selling period in the agreement for Pay for Sale?
If she is owed something, how much and from where?
Should the website's old End campaign button be removed?
situations.check: corrected: added the website's older End campaign button as a second way a brand can close things; removed the claim that the post's diary is a usable record

situations.title: The brand takes her content from the review screen and uses it without approving it — or after getting its money back
situations.stage: From the moment she submits her content for the brand's review, and any time after
situations.applies_to: Pay for Content mainly; also the social version she submits to the brand in Pay for Sale and Hybrid. Both modes.
situations.rules_ref: Section 12.2 lines 608, 619 and 624; section 26 lines 898 and 908. The situation itself is not in the rules.
situations.rules_say: Her files belong to that collaboration and only that brand and creator see them; approval locks the content; beyond the allowed rounds a rejection is a dispute. Nothing says what a brand may do with content it never approved, or content from a collaboration where its money was returned.
situations.today_entry_point: none. Her only report is 'the brand is silent', and only after she has posted — C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/contentFlow.service.js:786-791
situations.today_effect: Once she submits, the brand can open each original file through a five-minute link; nothing stops it being saved, there is no watermark, and the opening is noted only in the server log. If INFLX later returns the locked money to the brand, nothing happens to the files or to the brand's copies.
situations.money_at_stake: While in review 75% of her fee is locked with INFLX. If the brand reports and INFLX returns that money, she is left with the first 25% and the brand with her content.
situations.gap: A rule that unapproved content may not be used; a way for her to report it with proof; what INFLX does when the money has already gone back to the brand and nothing is locked.
possible_outcomes: Brand used it: INFLX treats the content as approved and releases what is locked to her
Money already returned to the brand: INFLX takes the fee from the brand's wallet by a written correction, if the balance is there
Brand is warned or suspended; the legal claim on her content stays hers
Prevention instead: low-quality or watermarked previews until the brand approves
open_questions: If a brand uses content it did not approve, is that the same as approving it?
When INFLX returns locked money to a brand in a dispute, may the brand keep or use what she submitted?
Do you want watermarked previews before approval?

situations.title: She posts the paid content without saying it is paid — or the brand asks her to hide that it is
situations.stage: When she posts on social media, and any time after
situations.raised_by: brand, creator, INFLX, or an outside complaint
situations.against: creator, or the brand if it asked her to hide it
situations.applies_to: All aims and both modes
situations.rules_ref: not in the rules (searched both rule documents for disclos, sponsor, paid partnership)
situations.rules_say: Silent. But clause 2 of the standard terms seeded for every agreement says content must 'comply with ASCI guidelines for sponsored content'; the published Creator Agreement makes the label a duty and repeating the failure a reason for suspension; the Brand Agreement lists 'asking creators to conceal a paid relationship'.
situations.today_entry_point: none of its own. The brand's general 'posted wrong' report, before it confirms, is the nearest thing.
situations.today_effect: Nothing checks it. Her live links are checked for the site name only and never opened, and INFLX's approval looks at the shop post inside INFLX, not at what she writes on Instagram or YouTube.
situations.money_at_stake: Pay for Content and Hybrid: 75% locked before the brand confirms, 50% during the wait. Pay for Sale: nothing locked.
situations.gap: Who checks the label and when; whether a missing label is fixable (edit the caption) or a breach that holds money; what happens when the brand told her to hide it. The standard terms actually live in production were not read — only version 1.0 as seeded.
possible_outcomes: She adds the label; nothing else changes
Missing label counts as 'posted wrong': the brand reports, the step freezes, she fixes it
Brand asked her to hide it: the brand is warned or suspended and she is paid as agreed
Repeat: the creator is suspended
open_questions: Will INFLX check for the paid label, or only act when someone complains?
Is a missing label a reason to hold payment?
What does INFLX do when the brand instructed it?

situations.title: The brand sells to her audience outside INFLX — in the store, on its own site, by phone — so her commission is never counted
situations.stage: After her posts are live
situations.applies_to: Pay for Sale and Hybrid; sharpest for Store Visit, where her followers can walk into the shop
situations.rules_ref: Section 16 lines 711-716; section 16A lines 733-735; Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md section 6.15 line 1100 (pay at store not built). Not in section 26.
situations.rules_say: Credit follows the shoppable post the shopper buys through, and every purchase goes through a post. Nothing about a sale made in the store or on the brand's own site after someone saw her content, or about a brand steering her followers there.
situations.today_entry_point: none
situations.today_effect: Only an order placed in the shopper app through her post carries commission. INFLX cannot see any other sale, nothing is recorded, and there is no code a shop counter could use to count one. It is her word against the brand's.
situations.money_at_stake: Nothing locked. Her commission on those sales and INFLX's own share are simply never created.
situations.gap: A plain sentence in the agreement that only orders placed through INFLX count (or a way to count store sales); whether a brand steering her followers away is a breach.
possible_outcomes: Not a dispute: only orders through INFLX count, and the agreement says so
A brand shown to be steering her followers away is warned or suspended
Later: a store code so counter sales can be credited to her
open_questions: Do sales in the store or on the brand's own site ever count for her?
Is a brand that pushes her followers to buy outside INFLX in breach?
Should the agreement say this in so many words?

situations.title: 'That wasn't me' — a signature, a confirmation or a withdrawal the account's owner later denies
situations.stage: Any time after signing: the signature itself, 'confirm it's live' (which pays money), a report, a withdrawal request
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes
situations.rules_ref: Section 9 line 431; section 2B lines 103 and 119; not in section 26
situations.rules_say: The signer types a full name and INFLX records the name, the moment, the device and the network address; the brand's signer is a person signing for the brand. A brand has one login number. Nothing about an action the owner later says someone else took. The published Terms forbid sharing an account and require authority to act for a business.
situations.today_entry_point: none
situations.today_effect: The evidence is kept: the typed name, time, device and network address of each signature, who pressed 'confirm live' and who filed a report, and every change of login number with the old and new number. But a brand has a single login, so a staff member and the owner look the same, and admin has no screen that shows these records.
situations.money_at_stake: The whole amount locked at the brand's signature, a second 25% released by a confirmation, or a withdrawal already paid to a bank.
situations.gap: A stated position (whoever holds the login acts for the account); an admin view of the signing record; what INFLX does when a number changed hands.
possible_outcomes: INFLX stands by the record: the action binds the account
Clear proof of a stolen phone or number: INFLX holds what is still locked and settles by hand
Separate logins for a brand's staff later, so actions carry a person's name
open_questions: Is every action from a logged-in account binding on its owner, full stop?
Should a brand be able to have more than one login?
What proof would make INFLX reverse an action?

situations.title: A creator turns out to be under 18
situations.stage: Any time after signing
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes
situations.rules_ref: not in the rules (section 2B lines 94, 102 and 111 list age only as a profile field that never blocks approval)
situations.rules_say: Silent. The published Terms say you must be 18 or older to use INFLX.
situations.today_entry_point: none
situations.today_effect: Age is not asked at registration, is not needed for approval, and is not looked at when she signs or when money is released. On the profile it is optional and accepts 13 to 99.
situations.money_at_stake: Whatever is locked for her collaborations plus the first 25% already paid; an agreement with a minor may not hold.
situations.gap: A minimum age and where it is asked; what happens to a running collaboration and its money if she is found to be under it; whether a guardian may sign.
possible_outcomes: 18+ confirmed at registration; an account found under age is suspended
A running collaboration is finished and paid, then the account is closed
A running collaboration is ended: work done is paid, the rest returns to the brand
open_questions: Is 18 the rule for creators, and should the app ask?
May a parent or guardian sign for a younger creator?
What happens to money already paid or locked?

situations.title: A brand or shopper reverses a card or UPI payment through the bank after INFLX has already used the money
situations.stage: Days or weeks after a wallet top-up or a shopper's online order
situations.raised_by: the payment company, on the payer's bank's instruction — INFLX is the one told
situations.applies_to: Pay for Content and Hybrid (a top-up that was locked and partly paid to her); shopper orders paid online (Pay for Sale and Hybrid)
situations.rules_ref: not in the rules (section 17A line 763 only says a top-up is credited once)
situations.rules_say: Silent.
situations.today_entry_point: none. The payment company's 'payment disputed' messages are not handled: the receiver lists the messages it knows and logs anything else as unhandled — C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/controllers/webhook.controller.js:598-614
situations.today_effect: Nothing is recorded and nothing stops: the wallet credit, the lock, her payments and a sale's three shares all carry on. INFLX would learn of it only from the payment company's own dashboard or email.
situations.money_at_stake: The top-up (possibly already locked, released to her and withdrawn) or the order amount (shares possibly already in the wallets). INFLX stands the loss unless it takes money back.
situations.gap: A place to record it; holding whatever is still locked or in the wallet; who bears the loss; the proof INFLX sends to contest it (signed agreement, delivery record).
possible_outcomes: INFLX contests it with the agreement and delivery proof and wins: nothing changes
INFLX loses: the brand's wallet is reduced by a written correction and the account suspended until it is made good
A shopper's reversed order is treated as unpaid: shares still waiting are cancelled
The creator keeps what she was paid for work done; INFLX carries the loss
open_questions: Who carries the loss when the money has already reached her and been withdrawn?
Is an account suspended at once when a payment is reversed?
Should INFLX wait some days before a new top-up can be locked or withdrawn?

not_disputes.title: A brand blocks a creator, or a creator blocks a brand, in the middle of a collaboration
not_disputes.why: Rules section 8A (lines 400-406) say a block only stops new pitches and invitations and is not retroactive: signed collaborations continue unchanged. The code does exactly that (blocks are read only by eligibility, discovery and brand search; the block itself carries no reason and admin has no screen for it). A block is a signal worth showing INFLX, not a dispute; if the blocker then goes silent, that is the 'stopped responding' dispute of section 26.

not_disputes.title: A brand's subscription plan lapses during a collaboration
not_disputes.why: Plan limits gate only creating a product, a campaign, a set and sending invitations (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/routes/campaign.routes.js:17,51,57,64 and brand.routes.js:118), and one admin switch can turn all limits off. Nothing after signing checks the plan, so a signed collaboration runs to the end. The rules are silent and nothing needs settling.

not_disputes.title: A shopper reports a comment on a post
not_disputes.why: This is moderation, not a broken agreement: the shopper reports, INFLX admin removes or keeps it, and pay never changes (posts rules 4.15, lines 601-607). It is built end to end and is a good pattern to copy. Loose ends: a report carries no reason, the commenter is never told or restricted, and the creator's own hide/reply (which the same rule promises) is not built, so neither she nor the brand can act on an abusive comment themselves (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/shopperEngagement.service.js:12-13).

not_disputes.title: An offer reaches its own end date, or a product sells out, and her posts leave the shop
not_disputes.why: The rules define this as the normal end of selling (master section 20; posts rules 4.9). Only the brand ending it early by choice is listed above as a possible dispute.

not_disputes.title: A brand or creator pauses pitches or invitations, or changes their settings, mid-collaboration
not_disputes.why: Section 8A line 406: changing settings is not retroactive and never touches signed collaborations.

not_disputes.title: Admin rejects a changed social account, or her numbers show 'not available'
not_disputes.why: This is the ownership check of section 2A working as designed. It becomes a dispute only if she has a signed collaboration at the time (see the handle-change situation).

not_disputes.title: She works with a competing brand at the same time
not_disputes.why: No exclusivity term exists: it is not in the terms a brand can set, not in the agreement, and not in the rules (searched for 'exclusiv' — found only an optional clause in the older contract PDF template, C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/pdf.service.js:178-183). The published Creator Agreement says she is free to work with other brands unless a signed term says otherwise (docs-parties.js:113). It could become a dispute only if you add such a term.

not_disputes.title: A brand tries to cancel a campaign after a creator has signed
not_disputes.why: Already closed: the old Cancel is refused once any collaboration carries both signatures, with the words 'If something has gone wrong, tell INFLX' (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/controllers/campaign.controller.js:1444-1463). The refusal is not a dispute; what the brand does next (goes silent, stops) is the section 26 dispute.

existing_machinery.name: Report-to-INFLX on the content and going-live step
existing_machinery.what: Brand and creator reports are saved on the collaboration with a kind, a note, who and when; a brand report freezes the step and the final-payment job skips a reported collaboration; both sides are notified. But no one at INFLX is alerted, the note is never shown again to anyone, and admin sees only a yes/no 'brand reported' mark on Money › Collaborations (a creator's report is not shown to admin at all). The natural base for new report kinds, once it has a reader.

existing_machinery.name: Admin can open the content files once a side has reported
existing_machinery.what: An admin-only link to view a collaboration's uploaded files, which works only after the brand or the creator has reported it to INFLX.

existing_machinery.name: Remote reports
existing_machinery.what: Three report stamps on a Remote shoot (difference in what arrived, problem with the return, return overdue) and the brand's report endpoint; recorded only — the code says dispute handling is item 18's.

existing_machinery.name: Admin money tools for settling
existing_machinery.what: Release the next locked payment to the creator, return what is still locked (including a waiting final 50%) to the brand, and add to or take from a wallet — each needs a written reason and is recorded. Telling is uneven: a release tells both sides and writes the diary; a return tells only the brand (the creator is not told); a balance correction tells nobody. None of them changes what the collaboration is called afterwards. The admin page is already titled 'Disputes and corrections'.

existing_machinery.name: Collaboration diary (written, not yet readable)
existing_machinery.what: One record that accepts entries from brand, creator, admin and the system, anchored to a signed collaboration or a shop post. Entries such as 'reported', 'confirmed live', 'payment released' and 'taken down' are being written, but the only screens and endpoints that read a diary are for the older pre-campaign conversation and pitch. It needs a reader (both sides and admin) before it can settle anything.

existing_machinery.name: 'Disputed' already has a name in three places
existing_machinery.what: The collaboration state families include a Disputed label, and the locked-payment status list includes 'disputed' (admin release refuses such a row, and 'End campaign' counts it as money still owed) — but no code ever sets either.

existing_machinery.name: No cancelling after both have signed
existing_machinery.what: The old Cancel campaign is refused once any collaboration carries both signatures, telling the brand 'If something has gone wrong, tell INFLX' — the natural place to hang a report entry.

existing_machinery.name: Comment report queue (report → admin decides)
existing_machinery.what: A complete small example of the pattern: a shopper reports, admin sees a queue with counts and oldest-first, decides Remove or Keep, and the decision is stamped with who and when. No reason on the report and nobody is told the outcome.

existing_machinery.name: Blocks
existing_machinery.what: Either side can block the other from the profile and unblock from a list; stored with who blocked whom and when, no reason, no admin view. Could carry an optional 'also tell INFLX why'.

existing_machinery.name: Suspend and reinstate
existing_machinery.what: Admin suspends an approved brand or creator and reinstates later; the person gets a push and SMS (without the reason) and the app locks their collaboration tabs. The reason is asked for on the screen but not required by the server, and it is wiped on reinstatement, so no history of past suspensions is kept.

existing_machinery.name: The one approved-account gate
existing_machinery.what: A single check that refuses every collaboration step (negotiation, agreement, shoot, Remote, content, going live, creator withdrawal) for an account that is not approved. It is the one place to decide what a suspended account may still do; today it does not cover the shop feed, checkout, the money jobs, brand withdrawals or brand order handling.

existing_machinery.name: Agreement snapshot and versioned standard terms
existing_machinery.what: Each signed agreement stores its own terms (including usage rights and her Instagram handle) and the version of INFLX's standard terms. Version 1.0 as seeded already says content must follow the sponsored-content guidelines and that disputes are 'resolved through the INFLX platform dispute resolution process'. New conduct clauses can be published as a new version without changing agreements already signed.

existing_machinery.name: Who signed, from where, and number changes
existing_machinery.what: Each signature stores the typed name, the time, the device and the network address; 'confirm live' and each report store who pressed them; every login-number change is kept with the old and new number. Evidence for 'that wasn't me' disputes, with no admin screen yet.

existing_machinery.name: Social account checks and measurement history
existing_machinery.what: Admin queue to confirm or reject a changed account, admin flags, and every measurement run kept with its numbers — the evidence base for a fake-numbers or handle-change complaint. Old store links keep working after a handle change.

existing_machinery.name: Post removal with a reason
existing_machinery.what: A post can leave the shop with a named reason and the creator is notified in plain words. Adding 'removed by INFLX' would reuse all of it (the list of reasons is fixed in the database and would need one more).

existing_machinery.name: Returns decision page
existing_machinery.what: Admin approves or rejects each shopper return or replacement with a note the shopper sees; the sale's shares wait while a request is open. The brand has a read-only list and no step of its own.

existing_machinery.name: Admin numbers with stamping
existing_machinery.what: Admin-set numbers with plain descriptions that are stamped on a collaboration when they first apply (change rounds, silence days, final-payment wait). The home for any new dispute clocks.

existing_machinery.name: Notifications
existing_machinery.what: One send function for in-app, push and optional SMS, used by every report and money tool above.

existing_machinery.name: Published legal pages and grievance form
existing_machinery.what: Terms, Creator Agreement, Brand Agreement, Delete My Account and Grievance pages already state conduct rules and promises (18+, no fake engagement, paid-post labels, 24-hour acknowledgement, 7-day resolution, payout holds, suspension reasons, closing an account from settings). The grievance form has no backend: it composes an email, so nothing is stored or numbered inside INFLX. The dispute rules should agree with these pages or the pages should be corrected.

result.area: Every waiting point after commitment, and what silence does (second reading, checked against code and rules v1.31)
result.summary: After signing (or after a shopper's Place order) there are about two dozen points where one side waits on the other or on INFLX. (a) Only four end by themselves: a Pay for Sale 'it's live' confirmation (7 days), a Remote return confirmation (7 days from reaching the branch, or from her 'I've sent it back'), the final 50% (7 days after the brand confirms) and sales money (when the return window closes after the brand marks Delivered). (b) Five give the waiting side a 'report to INFLX' button - products arrived different, return overdue, change rounds used up, posted wrong / missing / not posted, and brand silent after she posted (Pay for Content and Hybrid, from day 7) - but a report is only a saved date: nobody at INFLX is alerted, no Admin page lists it, nothing can close it, and a brand's content report freezes the step for ever. (c) Everything else has no time limit and no exit; some of it gets a 48-hour push (stopping at the posting date for the shoot, continuing for content) and some gets no push at all: a brand that has not sent a visit plan, an agreed visit time that has passed, a parcel or return in the courier's hands, INFLX reviewing a shoppable post (she is nudged instead), a brand shipping or marking a shopper's order delivered, INFLX deciding or refunding a return. On INFLX's own time the first reading was incomplete: besides the 24-hour withdrawal line, the legal pages inside all three apps and on the website promise every complaint is acknowledged within 24 hours with a reference number and resolved within 7 days, and the refund policy promises 'delivery is late - cancel for a full refund'; none of this has a timer, a queue or a reference number behind it (complaints arrive by email). Rules and app disagree in three places: the store visit 'confirms itself after 3 days' (retired 1 Oct), who escalates when change rounds run out (rules table: creator or system; app: brand only), and the two-round limit on INFLX sending a shoppable post back (not applied). The by-hand money tools exist in Admin; what is missing is the front half (raise, alert, list, hear the other side, time, decide, close) and an ending - today even after INFLX returns the locked money the collaboration stays open and the reminders keep coming.

situations.title: Someone reported to INFLX and INFLX has not answered
situations.stage: After any report or complaint. Type (c): INFLX has published promises on its own time, but nothing in the product times, lists or closes a report.
situations.raised_by: brand or creator (and, for orders, shopper)
situations.applies_to: All aims and modes
situations.rules_ref: Section 26 lines 892-909; section 22 line 844; section 12.2 line 632; section 17A lines 785-789. A time limit on INFLX: not in the rules - but it is in the published legal pages.
situations.rules_say: A report becomes a dispute that 'INFLX settles'; Admin may record the resolution and its money outcome; the detailed Admin dispute screen is deferred; settlement may be legal and outside the platform. In settling, INFLX may release a locked payment or return locked money, each with a written reason. The rules give no time - but the Grievance and Refund pages shown in all three apps and on the website promise: acknowledged within 24 hours with a reference number, resolved within 7 days, a refusal always answered.
situations.today_entry_point: none inside the product - nothing to chase, re-open or close a report with. Outside it: the website's complaint form, which only composes an email (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/Packages/brand-web/components/legal/GrievanceForm.js:116-117).
situations.today_effect: A report is a date on the step it was made in (five separate places). No INFLX staff are notified and no admin page lists reports; the written record of a signed collaboration exists but no screen or endpoint reads it. Nothing can mark a report settled or lift a freeze, so a brand's report stops the content step, Pay for Sale self-confirmation, the final payment and a return confirming itself, with no end. After INFLX returns the locked money by hand only the brand is told, every step stays open and the 48-hour pushes keep coming; a by-hand release of the final 50% does complete a Pay for Content collaboration, but a Hybrid one under a brand report can never read Completed. Meanwhile the brand can neither cancel nor end its campaign.
situations.money_at_stake: Whatever was locked when the report was made stays locked with INFLX; the brand cannot use it and she cannot receive it.
situations.gap: The whole receiving half: an alert, one list of open reports with a reference number, the other side's answer, a decision with a reason, a state that ends the collaboration and stops its reminders, and a clock on INFLX that matches what its own legal pages already promise.
possible_outcomes: Carry on: INFLX rejects the report, lifts the freeze, and the flow continues from where it stopped
Released to her: INFLX releases the next locked payment(s) with a reason (tool exists)
Returned to the brand: INFLX returns what is locked with a reason (tool exists); she keeps what was already paid
Split between them, if the founder allows it
The collaboration ends in a named state (for example 'Closed by INFLX') that both sides and the wallet show
open_questions: The legal pages already say 24 hours to acknowledge and 7 days to resolve - are these the clocks for collaboration disputes too, or should they have their own numbers?
Who decides (the founder alone for now?) and is there any appeal inside INFLX?
What is a settled collaboration called - Completed, or a separate ending - and does it still count in her profile's 'collaborations signed on INFLX'?
Should the other side always be told of a report and given a fixed time to answer before INFLX decides?
Do repeated reports against the same brand or creator lead to anything (a warning, a pause)?
