existing_machinery.name: Report fields on the content / going-live step
existing_machinery.what: Brand report (when, by whom, which of four reasons, a 500-character note) and creator report (when, by whom, note) are already stored per collaboration, one of each. Nothing clears or closes them.

existing_machinery.name: Report doors for both sides on content (phone only)
existing_machinery.what: Working endpoints and phone sheets: brand (rounds used, posted wrong, something missing, not posted) and creator (brand silent after the stamped date). The brand website has none.

existing_machinery.name: Report fields and door on the Remote shoot
existing_machinery.what: Three brand reports (products arrived different, return came back wrong, return overdue), each recorded once as a date, plus the 'It's fine, carry on' dismissal. Only two of the three have a phone button, the phone sends no note, and nobody is notified.

existing_machinery.name: The freeze
existing_machinery.what: One guard that refuses every action in the content step while a brand's report stands; reminders, Pay for Sale self-confirmation, completion and the final payment all already respect it. A dispute system needs only the matching 'unfreeze'.

existing_machinery.name: Stamped dates for every clock
existing_machinery.what: Each waiting period is copied onto the collaboration when it starts (report-from date, self-confirm date, final-payment date, return-confirm date, withdrawal hours), so changing a setting never moves a promise. A 'may report from' date for new cases can follow the same pattern.

existing_machinery.name: Admin settings with history
existing_machinery.what: The Platform settings page is data-driven: a new number (for example 'days before a silence can be reported', 'INFLX answers within') is one entry with range, description and an audit row per change. Today's waiting numbers: return window 7, return self-confirm 7, change rounds 2, brand silence 7, final payment wait 7, Pay for Sale self-confirm 7, withdrawals 24 hours; the shopper return window (7 days) lives under Money settings.

existing_machinery.name: The hourly lanes
existing_machinery.what: Hourly jobs already walk every signed collaboration: Delayed flags and Pay for Sale self-confirmation (:05), 48-hour reminders (:55), return self-confirmation (:15), the final payment (:00), and the two sales-money jobs (:01, :06). A 'report now open' or 'INFLX is late' check can ride these. No job watches shopper order status, post review or reports.

existing_machinery.name: One 'whose move is it' rule per step
existing_machinery.what: A single function per step says who must act and since when; Needs You, the reminders and the screens all read it. It is the natural place to work out 'silent for N days' - and it already shows the blind spots (nobody's move while a parcel is in transit, after a visit time is agreed, or while INFLX holds a post).

existing_machinery.name: The Delayed label with its stage
existing_machinery.what: Every signed collaboration past its posting date carries a date and the exact stage it stopped at, kept up to date as it moves. Ready-made evidence of where and since when something stalled - but no Admin page shows it today.

existing_machinery.name: The collaboration diary and the shoot log
existing_machinery.what: A dated record of who did what at each step (including 'reported', 'confirmed live', 'payment released by INFLX') is written for signed collaborations, and the shoot has its own action log (including a wiped 'attended' mark). This is the case file a dispute needs - but the diary is only readable today for the pre-signing conversation; nothing reads it by collaboration.

existing_machinery.name: Admin money tools for settling
existing_machinery.what: Release the next locked payment to the creator (optionally standing in for the brand's 'it's live'), return everything locked to the brand, and correct a balance - each needs a written reason, is recorded and guards against double clicks. A release tells both parties; a return tells only the brand; a correction shows only in the person's History.

existing_machinery.name: 'Settled by INFLX' is already understood by the apps
existing_machinery.what: Once INFLX has released or returned money by hand, the brand's Confirm is refused in plain words and both screens show what was returned and who confirmed (brand, automatic, or INFLX).

existing_machinery.name: Admin may open the disputed content (endpoint only)
existing_machinery.what: INFLX staff may fetch a collaboration's content files only once a side has reported - the privacy rule is enforced on the server. No Admin page calls it yet.

existing_machinery.name: Collaboration money list in Admin
existing_machinery.what: Every Pay for Content and Hybrid collaboration with what is locked, paid and due next, with tabs for 'Waiting on a brand' (showing days since she posted) and 'Due soon'. The data carries a 'brand reported' flag, but the list does not draw it (only the release dialog uses it) and the creator's report is not read at all.

existing_machinery.name: Shopper returns queue (the one working 'INFLX decides' flow)
existing_machinery.what: Request with reason and note, admins notified, approve / reject with a note the shopper reads, refund, money frozen while open, everyone told at each step. A good model for collaboration reports.

existing_machinery.name: Admin order tools
existing_machinery.what: INFLX can move a shopper's parcel status forward at any time, and cancel an item with a refund only while it is Confirmed or Packed (the same limit as the shopper).

existing_machinery.name: Withdrawals queue with a lateness flag and a menu badge
existing_machinery.what: Each waiting request shows how long it has waited and turns amber past its stamped hours, and the Admin menu shows a count. The only existing 'INFLX is late' signal, and a pattern for a reports queue.

existing_machinery.name: Published complaint promises and the complaint form
existing_machinery.what: The Grievance, Refund, Brand and Creator pages inside all three apps and on the website already state INFLX's clocks (acknowledge in 24 hours with a reference number, resolve in 7 days, a refusal is answered) and name who handles complaints; the website form composes an email. The words exist; the queue, reference numbers and timers do not.

existing_machinery.name: Notifications (push and the in-app bell)
existing_machinery.what: One sender used by every step, with the screen to open. Content reports already tell both parties in fixed words; Remote reports tell nobody.

existing_machinery.name: Unused 'disputed' states
existing_machinery.what: The database already allows 'disputed' on a locked payment and on an agreement, and the apps have a 'Disputed' label family; nothing sets them today.

existing_machinery.name: Old admin production queue
existing_machinery.what: An endpoint that still lists shoots that are stalled or Delayed, with reasons; its admin page was retired but the data is there.

not_disputes.title: No reply to an invitation, an unanswered counter, or an agreement not signed in time
not_disputes.why: All of these end as Expired at the Set's invitation cutoff (posting date minus 3 days), before both signatures exist. Nothing is locked and nobody is bound (rules section 25 lines 883-885; backend/src/jobs/set-expiry.job.js, negotiation-housekeeping.job.js, pitch-housekeeping.job.js, handshake-expiry.job.js).

not_disputes.title: The 'Delayed' label
not_disputes.why: It is a label for both sides, not a change of state: the collaboration stays in its Set, every step stays open and no money moves (rules section 25 line 889). It marks where a dispute may be hiding but is not one by itself.

not_disputes.title: Pay for Sale 'it's live' confirming itself after 7 days
not_disputes.why: Nothing is paid at that moment, so the brand's silence is ended by the system on the stamped date and both are told (rules section 12.1 lines 573, 581; backend/src/services/saleLive.service.js:443-486). Only a brand report turns it into a dispute.

not_disputes.title: A Remote return that reached the branch confirming itself after 7 days
not_disputes.why: The brand's silence is ended by the system on the stamped date and no money moves (rules section 25 line 888; backend/src/services/remoteJobs.service.js:28-96). (A return she only says she posted is different - see 'return booked but never arrives'.)

not_disputes.title: The wait for the final 50%, and the wait for sales money
not_disputes.why: Both are fixed waiting periods the system ends by itself: the final 50% on its stamped date, commission and the brand's share when the shopper's return window closes after delivery (tranche-3-release.job.js; commission-confirm.job.js; commerce-settlement.job.js).

not_disputes.title: An agreed store-visit time that passes once
not_disputes.why: The rules say nobody is blamed and nothing is recorded against either; the brand sends a new time (rules section 11.1 line 474). It becomes a dispute only if it keeps happening or one side goes silent - and note nobody is reminded when it passes.

not_disputes.title: The brand cancelling a parcel before the courier collects, or turning a Return item into a Gift
not_disputes.why: Normal buttons of the flow: the price and the return lock go back to the brand, or the item becomes hers (backend/src/routes/item11.routes.js:35, :39).

not_disputes.title: The creator flagging an item missing or damaged, and the brand tapping 'It's fine, carry on'
not_disputes.why: A recorded difference never stops her and is not a report; it becomes a dispute only if the brand chooses to report it (rules section 11.2 lines 520-523; backend/src/services/remoteReturn.service.js:141-152).

not_disputes.title: A shopper cancelling before the parcel ships, or the brand cancelling an item it cannot send
not_disputes.why: A normal ending with an automatic refund and all three shares reversed (Docs/OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md:1016-1036; backend/src/services/shopperOrders.service.js:421-509). It turns into a problem only if the refund itself fails.

not_disputes.title: A checkout whose online payment did not finish in 15 minutes
not_disputes.why: No order exists; the hold ends and the stock goes back (backend/src/jobs/checkout-expiry.job.js).

not_disputes.title: A withdrawal marked 'Could not process'
not_disputes.why: A normal ending: the reason is shown, the amount returns to Available and she may ask again (rules section 17A line 783; backend/src/services/withdrawalRequest.service.js:237-259).

not_disputes.title: INFLX sending a shoppable post back for fixing
not_disputes.why: The ordinary quality review loop: she fixes it and sends it again; the brand is not involved and her other posts are unaffected (rules section 12.1 line 563). Only an unlimited loop or an unanswered review is a problem.

not_disputes.title: A shoppable post approved after the posting date ('late'), or an approved post shown as 'not shared yet'
not_disputes.why: Both are labels the brand sees, with no penalty by rule (rules section 12.1 lines 564, 578; backend/src/services/saleLive.service.js:405-413).

not_disputes.title: Posts leaving the shop when the brand's offer ends or its products run out
not_disputes.why: By rule the post follows live product and offer availability; completion of the collaboration and the end of selling are separate (rules sections 19-20; backend/src/jobs/posts-offer-ended.job.js).

lifecycle.overall: The survey is thorough on the two-party failures: one side stops, goes silent, does it wrong, or disagrees about a fact. Walking the whole life again, the gaps that remain are of four kinds. First, the agreement itself is not single: the brand website can still add clauses, a bonus and a different mode, and rebuild the document with older wording, so the evidence every decision rests on can differ between the two sides. Second, things nobody did wrong have no place at all: illness, an offer that reaches its own end date while the shoot or INFLX's check ran late, a tick made before the damage was noticed, products that left the store with no record. Third, INFLX is never a party in its own system: its measured numbers, its changeable share of each sale, its 'Arrives by' date, its file limits, its clocks and its stand-in courier can all harm someone, and nothing records that the cause was INFLX or says whether INFLX makes it good. Fourth, the edges: a single stuck collaboration holds the brand's whole campaign open and its place cannot be refilled; a shopper has no door when the store misuses her number; and when the rules say 'outside the platform' the agreement may not even identify the other party and INFLX cannot hand over a case file. The rules and the product also disagree with each other in more than a dozen places that a dispute would turn on - store-visit self-confirmation, visits after the posting date, taking a shop post down, who holds cash, what the final 50% waits for, and what INFLX actually does with a dispute. Those need one answer each before any dispute screen is drawn, because whatever INFLX decides will be measured against the words already signed and published.

For a sale there is only 'Correct a balance', which leaves the sale itself still showing as waiting, so the job may add it again later (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/settlement.service.js:83,104-109).

contradictions.between: Her first 25% - the signing area versus the store-visit, remote, pay-for-content, money and admin areas
contradictions.detail: Five areas list 'also take the first 25% back from her wallet' as an outcome. Rule 17A line 786 says the first 25% 'has been paid', the Return dialog tells the admin her paid amount 'stays hers' (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/Packages/brand-web/app/admin/money/corrections/page.js:148), and section 22 line 844 sends non-performance to settlement outside the platform. One position has to be chosen before any tool.

contradictions.between: Unreturned products versus her payments - remote, money and admin areas versus the entry-points area and rule 11.2
contradictions.detail: Three areas offer 'hold her final 50% until the return is booked' and 'take the product's value from her fee or wallet'. Rule 11.2 line 537 says the return 'never holds up the content step or any payment', and lines 513 and 543 say the Creator is never charged. These outcomes need a rule change first, not just a tool.

contradictions.between: Does a return report stop the return confirming itself - admin area versus remote, money and time areas
contradictions.detail: The admin area says the job waits on a per-item mark that nothing writes. The job checks two things: that per-item mark (never written) and the shoot-level 'return reported' stamp, which the report door does write (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/remoteJobs.service.js:33-35,47; C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/remoteReturn.service.js:121-133). So a 'return' report does stop self-confirmation - but the phone has no button that sends it.

contradictions.between: The return hold when every Return item is marked missing - entry-points area versus remote area
contradictions.detail: Entry-points says the hold goes back to the brand; the remote area says it stays held. The code releases it only from the brand's 'turn into a Gift' action (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/remoteReturn.service.js:233 is the only caller); her item check does not (remoteReturn.service.js:42-100). The remote area is right, and rule 11.2 line 536 is not met.

contradictions.between: The return due date when the shoot is never marked done - remote area versus signing area
contradictions.detail: The remote area reads the rule as giving a due date from the posting date; the signing area says the rule assumes she marks the shoot. The code works out a due date from the posting date but calls it overdue only once the shoot is marked (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/remoteShoot.service.js:156-161,170), so the brand's 'overdue' report never opens for a silent creator.

contradictions.between: Cash on delivery - master rule 17A, the second rules document, the brand website and the code
contradictions.detail: 17A line 777: INFLX collects the cash and the brand owes nothing. OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md lines 1081-1084 and the brand website (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/Packages/brand-web/app/dashboard/fulfillment/page.js:333): the brand collects and the shares are taken from its next payout. The code follows 17A (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/settlement.service.js:53-55) while a comment elsewhere still describes cash dues nothing creates (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/remoteMoney.service.js:135-137). Today nobody takes the shares from the brand.

contradictions.between: 'Self-dealing costs INFLX nothing' (people area) versus the cash-on-delivery finding (shopper and money areas)
contradictions.detail: The people area calls a creator who owns the brand 'mostly the owner paying herself'. On a cash order that is wrong: the brand marks its own order Delivered and, after the window, INFLX credits the brand's share and the commission from its own money (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/settlement.service.js:94-119; C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/jobs/commission-confirm.job.js:36-42,91-98). Cash is on by default up to Rs 5,000 a checkout (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/shopperCheckout.service.js:41-42), so a brand and creator together can turn made-up cash orders into withdrawable balances.

contradictions.between: Delivery fee and cash fee - the second rules document versus the code
contradictions.detail: OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md line 1075 says both fees go to the brand. The code stores them on the parcel and credits them to nobody (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/shopperCheckout.service.js:409-422; C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/settlement.service.js:98-119). No area raised it because both are zero today.

contradictions.between: Holding a payout during a complaint - outcomes in the signing, people and money areas and the published legal pages, versus rule 17A
contradictions.detail: Several outcomes ('her withdrawals wait while a complaint is open') and the public pages ('INFLX may hold a payout while it investigates') need a hold. 17A line 782 says a withdrawal has 'no approval or rejection step' and is processed within 24 hours, and the code has none (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/withdrawalRequest.service.js:16).

contradictions.between: Which rule governs a creator who does not perform - sections 22 and 26 versus 17A
contradictions.detail: Section 22 line 844 and section 26 line 895 say settlement is outside the platform with INFLX recording it; section 26 line 908 speaks only of releasing the locked 75% to the Creator; 17A line 787 says INFLX may release or return. Every area assumed 17A.

contradictions.between: 'A brand report holds the final payment' (signing, money and admin areas) versus the pay-for-content area
contradictions.detail: The job would skip a dated final payment under a brand report (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/contentMoney.service.js:95-97), but a report can only be made before confirmation, when no final payment has a date (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/contentFlow.service.js:775-779). So a report never holds a final 50% that already has its date; the pay-for-content area has it right.

contradictions.between: What 'INFLX sides with the creator' ends as - admin area versus sale and money areas
contradictions.detail: The admin area says release both payments and it ends Completed. That is true for Pay for Content only, and it reads 'Completed' even when the content was never approved or posted (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/contentMoney.service.js:128-137). A Hybrid collaboration under a report never completes (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/saleLive.service.js:326), and Pay for Sale has no money tool at all.

contradictions.between: Tax at withdrawal - the two rules documents
contradictions.detail: OFFER_TERMS_POSTS_RULES.md line 1078 still says TDS is deducted when she withdraws (Rs 100 becomes Rs 90). Master section 17 line 752 and the code (C:/WORK/inflx-platform/backend/src/services/withdrawalRequest.service.js:16-17) say nothing is deducted. It matters whenever a disputed amount is worked out.

money.overall: Every pocket of money was walked: brand Available, the locked fee and its three payments in each state, the campaign fee, courier charges and the return hold, product value, the shopper's payment, a sale's three shares before and after the window, pending and confirmed commission, money on hold for a withdrawal, money already paid to a bank, and cash on delivery. INFLX can move a collaboration's locked money in exactly two shapes today - the next whole payment to her, or everything left back to the brand - and can add to or take from one wallet's Available. Every other outcome the areas name (a split of another size, a pause, an undo, a deduction, a transfer between the two, a refund after payout, anything at all on Pay for Sale) either cannot be done or can only be imitated with balance corrections that are not tied to the case. None of the tools ends a collaboration: after a return it can never become Completed, keeps its reminders, and the creator is not even told. Money that has left a wallet cannot be reached: a take never goes below zero, cannot touch a withdrawal that is On hold, and only brands have an 'owed' record, for courier charges only. The brand side has the same hole in reverse: on Pay for Sale INFLX holds nothing of the brand's, so any award against a brand is words. For shopper orders the tools stop at two walls - once Shipped nobody can refund, and once the shares are in the wallets the app refuses and points to Money, which cannot reverse INFLX's own share or send the refund. The largest live exposure is cash on delivery: the brand's own 'Delivered' tap makes INFLX pay the brand and the creator from its own money, and a brand and creator acting together can abuse it. New pockets no area listed: a referral reward paid from INFLX's share and never reversed, delivery and cash fees that belong to nobody, the payment provider's charges on money that goes back, courier prices charged while the courier is a stand-in, and wallet money created while payments are in test mode. Several proposed outcomes also conflict with the rules as written (her first 25%, her payments versus unreturned products, holding a withdrawal), so they need the founder's decision before any tool is built.
